evidence.excerpt: Which brings us to anti-racism. If it is not simply the absence of a racist feeling, what is it? I would describe anti-racism as the deliberate practice of identifying, challenging, preventing, and changing racial inequities in relationships, organizations, and systems. The word deliberate does a lot of work. Think about workplace safety.

If a private company makes a confusing form, that is frustrating. chapters.title: Sustaining the work through ordinary decisions

evidence.excerpt: So what is anti-racism? It is not a claim that every white person is bad. It is not permission to stereotype. It is not a substitute for evidence, legality, competence, or individual dignity. It is the practice of looking honestly at how racial inequity can be produced, including through ordinary systems and then changing what can be changed.
